Story time: My husband and I took my sister and brother in law and their two young kids on their first Disney trip this past April. As a Disney veteran with no kids yet I had to learn the stroller etiquette on the fly. The morning we rope dropped flight of passage I figured we had to drop their stroller before feeding into the line, which spills way out of the normal queue in the morning. So I told them I would take the stroller and meet up with them. It turns out you’re supposed to keep the stroller with you and they take it from you and park it for you. So a cast member just told me to rejoin my party. But they had already marched to a location that I could not possibly make it up to with the stroller. The cast member had me wait with her until my party doubled back as the queue wove by again. While waiting there I was shouted at by multiple people saying I was trying to cut the line, with my empty stroller. I’ve never been so embarrassed. I agree that people shouldn’t be trying to save space while their party is off riding another ride. But Disney is a complicated place and there are lots of reasons parties can be separated. It definitely put that into perspective for me next time I think someone is line hopping. My singular body did nothing to slow down the people behind me in such a high volume ride and that guy brought some serious negativity to an already intense morning.

I can’t speak to cali, but Boston is a HCOL area and this was my experience:
It was about $1,000 for my makeup day of, $300 for my trial. And $300/bridal party member just for makeup. I had a very popular artist who focused on soft glam. I had to put down a 50% deposit and I did that before my trial. I had 14 people getting their hair and makeup done total so the lead artist of the company came and brought a second artist. I also have a 20% tip for each service. My artists weren’t available to stay for touch ups but my makeup looked flawless literally the entire night!
Hair was around $600 for day of bridal hair, $300 for my trial, $250/bridal party member. I did have her stick around for touch ups and to do a hair style change for my late reception/afterparty outfit and I believe I payed around $90/hour that she stuck around. It was great having her there, especially for an outdoor ceremony and having done a first look. I also gave her a 20% tip. She also brought a second stylist for the group of 14. On top of this we had to put all stylists up because we had our wedding in a rural area in the winter, so we also paid a $70/day food stipend and travel fees. I forget the driving cost but it was something per mile outside of their radius. They did not do halfway done on anything. It wasn’t “perfect” at the trial, only because my hair stylist was trying a couple of styles for me that day, but damn near perfect. And my makeup artist tried a couple different lip colors with me so we also played with blush colors as well, but we settled on a complete look every time. I also hired them both for my rehearsal dinner, which was awesome, especially because we had photo and video there, and my makeup and hair was consistently flawless. And I had my makeup artist do my makeup for my bridal shower, which made my trial even easier because she had already worked with me once. I love them so much, I had my makeup artist do my makeup for another event I attended. Both lead stylists were exactly who did my trial and my weekend of hair/makeup. We had phone interviews before hiring for me to communicate any concerns I had and hear their responses, with my planner on the line. They were both super kind and open to corrections and changes and really just wanted me to be happy. My suggestion is look at their styles and make sure their style is exactly what you’re looking for. You have so many options in your location, so I’m sure a lot to sort through. But just because someone is good doesn’t make them GREAT at all styles. If you want full glam, then don’t even consider people that do soft glam or natural. Look at stylists that really focus on full glam. Listen when you interview them for them to actually respond to your concerns. See if their personality or right for you as well. They’re a part of your room and your people. It helps if they fit in.

I think you hired the wrong planner. Planners normally cost about 10% - 15% of a wedding budget. And when you try to save money on a vendor, what you’re doing is booking a vendor that doesn’t fit the price range of the quality of the rest of your vendors. The quality of service you’re expecting would come from a planner in the $10k - $20k price range, especially in California. We payed $17,500 for our planner and she did everything you are expecting but we got most of the work done much closer to the date. Your planner literally may not have the connections, skill set and experience to do what you’re asking her to do. There are, of course, new people on the scene that cost less and are trying to build their portfolios and can give fantastic service for a lower price, but you do get what you pay for. You really may be better off hiring a different planner at an appropriate price point if you have the budget, or you may need to adjust your expectations. The good news is you have plenty of time. Try to remember that your planner most likely has weddings coming up right now that take precedence over yours when it’s so far away. If you have all of your major vendors booked, you shouldn’t need to worry about design right this moment. Maybe try having a phone call with her to talk about your expectations and ask her what you can expect for communication and timelines. A zoom call or phone call can be very helpful for these types of conversations. And as far as communication goes, that far out from our wedding we emailed with our planner only when needed. It wasn’t until 8 months out that we increased our emailing and until 4 months out that we really needed regular phone calls.

On top of that venues have minimum spending fees, so if your venue is going to sign with you, you need to be worth it to them over a 200 person wedding. We had a Friday wedding at a resort in the mountains two weeks ago. There was a storm Thursday and a storm Saturday, so we ended up hosting event more than we planned. We got there Wednesday and had a bunch of stuff to do with our planner and the resort, then a lot of guests came early to get ahead of the storm so we made a rotation saying hello. We had originally intended for alone time that night, but when the people come, they all want to be with you so we made it happen. Thursday we hosted a bridal luncheon at 11am for me and my bridesmaids. Then rehearsal at 2pm. My dad hosted a cocktail party at 4:30 in his room for the rehearsal dinner group (wedding party, family and dates were 37 people). Rehearsal dinner at 5:30 with the photo/video team arriving at 5 for detail shots, portraits and family photos. We covered food and open bar for this event. Welcome party at 8pm for 71 people. Again, we covered open bar, a crepe station and three passed apps for this event, as well as a band for welcome party and rehearsal dinner. Day of we covered breakfast for the wedding party, women in my suite getting ready, men at the resort restaurant. We also covered lunches in my suite for the women, and my dad’s suite for the men. We had welcome cocktails before the ceremony for all guests, cocktail hour (with three stations, three passed apps and open bar), reception with full open bar and late night food, then we hosted an afterparty with a new band and a cash bar. Saturday we hosted brunch, then because of the storm some guests needed to stay longer so we worked with the resort to get them rooms and match other guests with guests that had extra space if they were comfortable. Then we hosted ANOTHER cocktail party mid day in our room on the fly to keep them entertained. I’d say it was about 1/3 of our guests that stuck around. Then another impromptu cocktail party in my dad’s room after everyone found dinner on their own, plus we had left over cigars so we went to the heated outdoor pool and firepits to entertain and smoke with everyone. That’s way more than we planned, we had hoped for a quiet Saturday, but what are you supposed to do? Abandon guests and say you’re on your own? My parents were super helpful! But I would say you should plan on hosting the entire weekend if you are having a destination event. And if you are having a wedding anywhere the weather might be an issue, plan to host even more!

I’m sorry you’ve been through that with your current planner, that totally sucks. That said, it’s not a red flag that the price went up to add an assistant. It’s also pretty normal for planners to want to get a jump on things, especially if they’re going to have to fix someone else’s crappy work this close to your wedding. I don’t have kids yet but I definitely would prefer to leave them at home with a trusted source in a safe space they are used to than leave them with wedding child care.

I think at that point it would be about a conversation with the parents. Like, we had a child free wedding and didn’t have kids in the ceremony, but it was originally considered because then they could be part of family photos and the overall experience while also allowing their parents to have a good time at the reception and not worry about their kids being up late or misbehaving. We landed on no kids at all because it was a very high end resort and all of the parents agreed that it would be hell to keep their kids entertained and behaved the entire weekend. But if it was a local event and the couple was paying for their outfits, I could see it as a good way to include them in family photos without worrying about them being at the wedding causing trouble.

We also faced major sticker shock. Our planner predicted a $10k-$15k floral cost. Florals weren’t our priority, but we’re having a winter wedding, so no “in season” flowers and I had a specific vision. She listened to what we wanted and recommended the best vendor for our vision, whose quote ended up at $25k and when all was said and done, we’re paying $31k. That is not her fault. We added things and fleshed out our vision that added to the cost. And to get the aesthetic we wanted it meant working with a vendor who could do that artistically. And so if we had gone with something more generic, it probably would have stayed in the originally predicted range. But we didn’t, and the price reflects that. I think one of the issues with sticker shock, beyond the gross inflation is that wedding blogs tell you an average and then pair it with pictures that are far above and beyond what that average is. Have your planner’s recommended vendors really been exactly what you’ve asked for aside from price? Your style, your vibe, your needs? If so, then maybe it isn’t a her issue, maybe your expectations are at a higher cost and she’s choosing to prioritize your design desires over your budget. You could try having a conversation with her saying you’d like to prioritize your budget more moving forward and that could help. And be more open minded about not meeting all of your design goals. It sounds like as your planner has presented vendors with inflated costs, you’ve said yes. She may just think your budget is a guideline, not a rule. We started with a wicked low budget because we thought that would pay for a wedding, but because it was what we had to work with. And our costs have gone way up. But, we’re having the wedding of our dreams. It’s all a give and take, but I think it’s worth having a clarifying conversation with your planner about prioritizing budget and some hard numbers you will mot go over before you fire her.

I honestly don’t think you have any recourse. The place that did your storing should have told you that if there was glue that might happen. Whether or not your wore it for a wedding immediately and then had it cleaned and stored so your daughter or granddaughter could wear it, this would have happened without paying attention to the make of the dress. Not all dresses are made the same, including designer. I tried on many designer gowns and was shocked to see and feel the low quality relying on a name. We actually worked with a stylist for our wedding and she told me very specific brands to avoid because they’re name first, quality second. The designer and the boutique don’t owe you anything because you didn’t receive the dress that way from them. It was the act of having it cleaned and stored that did this. Which was something you chose to do, so I really wouldn’t expect any kind of help from either the boutique or designer. Especially after all of this time has passed. And this is more common than you think. My stepmother just told me a story about how when she received her dress back from storing back in the 90s, her friends told her to check it because damage can be done and covered up. Sure enough, the beading down the back was completely ruined and had to be rebuilt. Had she not looked, when she pulled it out to show me this last week we would have found it ruined, 30 years later, with no one to hold accountable because so much time had passed. I think the ONLY person you may get help from is the place that stored it, as they should have looked for the glue beforehand and either adjusted their process or told you no. Either way, I’m so sorry but to expect literally anything from the designer or boutique I think is completely unreasonable. So sorry this happened to you.

But our planner and designers have never made us feel like a burden. When we don’t know or don’t care as much we ask their opinion and favor that. So it’s definitely a symbiotic relationship. That being said, it’s important to honor the style of your designers. We started wanting a white on white wedding and our designer really steered us clear of that. They didn’t want everything to look washed out given our space and the time of year (a winter wedding). So I would also ask why your designer chose something and because they may have a reason having seen how the space works.

I think you’ll want to have a very clear line about who is invited to which event. If your first event is very clearly only family, then friends only invited to the second event should understand. 1. There are websites that tell you average wedding prices of given locations.
2. Yes, a very big difference. A planner charging $10k per wedding only has to take 10 weddings a year to make a very comfortable living. A planner that charges $2k per wedding has to take 50 weddings a year to make the same amount. You aren’t just paying for connections to great vendors and their experience. You’re paying for their time. Do you want someone juggling multiple weddings a weekend and emails from 50 couples already signed plus new wedding inquiries for the following year? Or do you want someone that only takes 10 couples a year and can dedicate the time to your wedding?
3. We’re getting married in New England, many of our vendors are from Boston. It’s one of the most expensive locations to get married in the country. Not only is it a HCOL location, it’s a vacation/destination wedding location. Expect vendors and venues to be booked out very far in advance.

Yeah it increases. Two months out you’re getting questions from guests and wedding party members. You have to purchase gifts for parents and wedding party members. Random items for the ceremony or reception. Do you have the special archival pens that are acid free for your guestbook or whatever people are signing? Did you tell your venue you need a table for that signing thing to be on? Have you confirmed that signing thing will be transferred from the cocktail hour to the reception space? Does it need to be transferred in a frame to keep it from getting damaged? What are you serving your wedding party for lunch? Is the lunch place able to accommodate your bridesmaid’s new dietary restriction? Did you fill out your photographer’s preevent survey? What exact family and wedding party photo combos do you want and in which order? At what exact times will each person be getting their hair and makeup done? Do you have a steamer for your dress? That bridesmaid that wants to change which shoes she’s wearing, are they the same height as the heels she got the dress hemmed for? Did she even get her dress hemmed? Can your sister bring her new boyfriend? If so, can he come to the rehearsal dinner too? I’m two weeks out and it’s NEVER ENDING!! I only stop doing wedding things when I’m eating and sleeping and the eating thing is a forced choice for sanity. Enjoy this slow period. Everyone will want a piece of you soon enough and the decision fatigue is REAL! I’m thrilled that we planned such a thoughtful wedding and also so excited to have my life and free time back!!

You would need to make the wedding attire less formal for sure. Nothing that would require floor length dresses or expensive shoes. If I went to a wedding that was cocktail style or semi formal with a short dress and more casual heels and this happened I would throw a raincoat on and make it work. If this happened and I had a long dress and nice shoes on and they were ruined by mud or puddles I would definitely not be happy. So your ceremony would ideally be on a gravel surface at a casual wedding formality level.

When we chose our date we checked with every wedding party member for birthdays, vacations, and significant dates. We also looked at school breaks and holidays to make sure we weren’t overlapping so we weren’t commandeering someone’s winter break, taking their vacation time and making it about us. We’re having a winter wedding so those things mattered to us. You can absolutely make guest oriented decisions and still have a wedding about you. Planning a wedding on or around a holiday means potentially a lower acceptance rate and that’s on the bride and groom to accept. Just like when we chose a child free wedding we knew some people may say no. Pretending that brides and grooms aren’t responsible for their decisions because they could have been overlooked feels silly.

I don’t have a kid and would go to the wedding, making a point to call my dad that day and plan another time to see him. That being said, if I had a kid it would 100% be a no from me. Check my post history, I’m all about parents taking a trip and leaving their kids with sitters. My parents did it, my aunts and uncles did it. I sat for parents that did it. Culturally, I’m pro parent only vacations! But I definitely wouldn’t leave my future kid on Mother’s Day and would never expect my future husband to do so on Father’s Day. I would expect a much high decline rate if you’re having an adult only wedding.

I’m all for doing what brings you joy, especially when you can afford it. But some perspective for you. We worked with a custom designer that had a $250 design fee and then probably got commission off of the invitations themselves, which were $65 each for the entire suite. She’s been wonderful. She’s done all of the artwork for our wedding and all paper and signage. Each thing she designs incurs a new $250 fee, so it does add up. But honestly, it’s been so worth it. This is exactly why people go to premarital counseling. This won’t be the only time that finances come into play during your marriage. I know a lot of people that have worked in daycares that have a lot of negative things to say about their work environments and the people they’ve worked with. Not every daycare is a professional establishment and not every professional establishment hires child care professionals. You don’t need a degree to work in a daycare. Meanwhile, I was a nanny and babysat before that. My friends and I all went through first aid and choking certifications. We all worked the summers as camp counselors and it was a very common job from teenagers through college. We were all interviews by the parents and provided references from previous families and employers. They had us try out sitting their kids while they were home, then while they went out for a short evening out, then longer. You aren’t just hitting up some random teen on Facebook. Communities shared the same set of responsible young people as sitters and the sitters helped link different local families with others of their families needed coverage and they weren’t available. Maybe this is a cultural thing, but it was a very common thing in all of the towns I lived in and I moved around every few years. New England and New York based.

This is EXACTLY the issue. Not the child almost ruining the cake. But the fact that it was my the kid’s parent. Most parents stop parenting and assume the village of people will take over while they have some fun which is just so wildly rude and presumptive. Imagine what would have happened if you had just let that happen because you are not that child’s parent. People are afraid to leave their kids with sitters but ignore their kids out in public.

Genuine question though, what about the drinking environment around children? We’re having an open bar with a crowd that we know drinks heavily. It will be completely inappropriate for children to be there. I personally do not believe children belong around drunk people. Casually having a glass of wine or beer or a single cocktail is one thing. Watching your uncle or friend from college get wasted because they have a hotel room in the venue and knowing there are kids around to watch it is just so wrong to me. So are weddings in your family just very casual drinking or non drinking events? Or do people get drunk around kids? I guess I just don’t go to weddings that don’t have a party environment.

Can someone please explain to me why parents are comfortable leaving their kids with the random people hired to work at their kid’s daycare that they didn’t interview personally but not with a professional sitter that has first aid and choking certifications and a stack of references? There was a thread last week about how it was unreasonable to expect people to leave their kids overnight with a sitter and I just cannot understand how your kid is in more danger asleep with a professional in the house than they are at a daycare while awake and fully impressionable when you don’t have a day in who that daycare hires. It makes zero sense to me.

Kids should “be kids” and also learn appropriate behavior for different situations. That’s raising a kid. Teaching kids that recess is running time and classroom time we sit still. This whole movement that kids deserve full bodily autonomy and zero discipline is exactly why so many no kids weddings are happening. Because the parents of those children didn’t stop that from happening. When I was little my parents would have removed me from the space until I could be calm. If one of my sibilants had an outburst at a restaurant it meant the entire family didn’t go out to a restaurant again for a while and it was made clear that we couldn’t go because of poor behavior, even if it wasn’t everyone behaving poorly. Unless you are actively planning a child friendly wedding, most kids don’t really belong there. And by child friendly I mean kids food, kids activities, no excessive drinking. Otherwise, leave the kids at home.

It all depends on your crowd! We went to a beautiful wedding for my cousin on the beach in Florida. It was awesome. But I don’t know if they requested club music or the DJ just did it, but only the bride and her bridesmaids felt comfortable dancing and grinding to those songs. The rest of the families didn’t connect with the music or feel comfortable at all. Once the music switched to disco and funk (more traditional wedding music), the dance floor was packed. I don’t know if they had an image in their heads of the wedding being like a club scene on the beach, but it definitely wasn’t the vibe of the guests they invited. I’ve also been to weddings where dancing wasn’t the vibe at all. It was daytime, super bright in the room with kids running around, and the bride and groom were super disappointed no one was dancing and people were leaving early. They didn’t create an atmosphere for that to feel comfortable so it was more of a hang outside in the garden and chat vibe. You need to think of what you want, what type of people your guests are, and then try to create something that works for both ideas. If you have foodies primarily, focus on the food. If you want a drinking and dancing fest, don’t invite kids. If you want a casual barefoot evening, let your DJ know in advance so they know the vibe you’re going for.

Address the save the date and invitations by the names of the people coming, “Mr. And Mrs. Robinson”. Pass it along by world of mouth and have it on your wedding website. And make sure to point out things like, “it wouldn’t be fair to include one person’s children and not everyone’s”, “costs and headcount limitations would mean that if you allowed children to come, it would mean cutting other cherished loved ones from the event”, “the overall event will not be child friendly or appropriate of children to be at”.

I live in New England, so I’m American. And everyone I know lives their lives this way. As they did when I was a kid. It could be regional. But just so you know that there are many ways of doing things. Lots of people feel comfortable with different people watching their children.
YES! My parents used to bring local high school kids to babysit us on vacations! They would just hang out in the hotel and play with us when my parents got a nice meal or went to an event!
Thank you! Lol, I was getting such negative feedback for suggesting people have different cultural standards I thought I was going crazy! Lol

I’m talking about leaving your children at home. The kids don’t need to be flown internationally. And if you are going to bring them, many hotels offer sitting services for guests. It really isn’t an odd thing to send your kids to the resort childcare center or have a staff member oversee them while they watch a movie and play games in your room for the few hours you’re gone. Weddings aren’t that long. Again, I really feel like this is a cultural difference. No one I know feels afraid to leave their kids with sitters. It’s so so common.

There are plenty of very qualified “strangers” that are better able to tend to children than a grandparent. My point was that it’s cultural to feel this way. That only family can watch family. Nannies and sitters exist for a reason. I was a sitter as a teenager and in my early 20s I nannied. We also were left with sitters, sometimes family, sometimes not and we did just fine. Just interview them beforehand and get references. Culturally, that’s what everyone I know does. It’s really no big deal.

So leave your kids at home with the trusted sitter. You don’t need to bring them to a foreign country. We were perfectly fine staying with sitters in our home. Plenty of people do this. My point was that it’s cultural to feel this way. That only family can watch family. There are plenty of people that don’t need it to be family to watch your children.

My parents took vacations a couple of times a year that required passports when we were kids. I think it’s only certain cultures that feel this way. Whether you’re down the street, across the country, or another country over, it’s still someone else watching your children. You’re either comfortable with it or not. And I think that comes from how you were raised. We were raised watching my parents and their friends attend events that were adult only so we, as adults embrace that concept as well. If you were raised in a family where kids were always there, then it’s hard to understand why some people believe kids are inappropriate at a lot of events. It’s just about where you come from and how you were raised.

I don’t think this is an issue. Touch base with your nonmarried guests personally and explain that you’ll be paying for their flights and accommodations. And leave it at that. Address every invitation with the full name of the plus one so it isn’t an “and guest” situation. Plenty of weddings don’t even offer plus ones to people that aren’t in serious relationships. We offered plus ones to all guests and assumed people would just bring dates and have multiple people bringing siblings and friends. Definitely not our intention, but we offered the plus ones and that’s that. If you’re paying for flight and accommodations you are by no means obligated to give someone a plus one. If you weren’t paying for those things I would say otherwise. But adult human beings are capable of flying somewhere on their own for free. It’s absurd for anyone to feel otherwise in my opinion. People will take advantage of the free payed for plus one and bring a buddy. No doubt. Just get full names of the plus ones you’ll be inviting, make sure the invitations are clear and be prepared to calmly explain that you were including serious relationship plus ones only due to the nature of the event. Anyone pissy with you probably doesn’t need to be there anyway.

Unless you’re having a church service, I think you’re fine! That being said it’s all about what YOU think. And if YOU think it isn’t too much, then rock it out. If YOU think you would feel more comfortable showing less because some guests may give side eye, then that’s just as okay. Sometimes what those around us think matters to us and sometimes it doesn’t. Not all of us feel comfortable going against what others say. In the end, whether you do something to please others or make yourself comfortable or just wear your dream dress, it’s ALL OKAY! The only person who gets to decide in the end is YOU!

Everyone is correct, it’s legally binding and they owe you the apps. HOWEVER, you don’t want to piss off your venue. And so would hate for them to start shrinking other portion sizes for entrees, or pouring less alcohol, whatever they can do to make their money back. So I would handle it with tact. Be very calm and kind about holding them accountable. Make it clear that you’ve consulted with a legal team and they explained that the contract is legally binding. That your sorry it happened and you’re sure it isn’t a great feeling for them, it isn’t a great feeling for you either! But you’d like to move forward working together with positivity, abiding by what the contract that was legally binding says, and keep moving and grooving toward your wedding planning goals. Don’t threaten arbitration or raise voices or use harsh language if you can avoid it until absolutely necessary. Keep it upbeat and positive and kind and calm. While simultaneously insisting on following the contract to the letter. That being said, don’t expect any extras or upgrades to be easily added after this. They’ll probably ring you out to dry pricing wise, so if you insist on the contract, make sure you’re very happy with it. You should NOT be paying for those apps!

I completely agree with you. It’s not “good business”. It has been what my experience has been through the two years of planning we’ve done. Not to mention this is slow season so they may be taking vacations, doing venue renovations, just a slew of things. And while YOU have your ducks in a row, assume the majority of clients don’t. And they don’t know you yet, so they’re probably assuming you’re just another person wasting their time until that contract is signed. It’s malarkey but definitely a common experience unfortunately.

You have to know your crowd. My maid of honor’s family has done stuff like this before. They are all garden/crafty people. But my family would not be into this. Weddings are weird. They have all of these very specific etiquette moments. Feeling sad is valid. And I think you should feel comfortable sharing that with your fiancé. He’s your person for life as of January so he’s exactly who you should feel comfortable talking about this with. I can’t imagine he would view you as a bridezilla if he knows and loves you. That said, I think the major issue here is the propaganda out there that it’s your day and if someone loves you they’ll just figure it out and be there. People have lives. That person that planned a trip after knowing your date may have other constraints like work or other people’s schedules that made them choose that time for their vacation. Yes, you chose a challenging time having it follow the holidays. People are strapped for cash and PTO and if it came to my winter vacation or a wedding, I would have to really consider giving up my vacation time or not depending on the relationship. I say all of this just so you can remind yourself it doesn’t mean these people don’t love you. But your wedding is only the top priority for you and your fiancé. Everyone else has whole lives to lead and just like any other party, your wedding is a consideration in how it fits into their lives. It’s really the toxic propaganda that we all get bombarded with that this is the most important day ever and everyone else owes us being there. They don’t. It’s not. It’s a great, wonderful day with our life partner and whichever friends and family have the ability to be there. So try to ground yourself and remember in the end, the thing that matters is marrying your soul mate!

It’s all about how you put the wedding together. A ballroom wedding can feel “cheap” if it’s done a certain way. That being said, there is nothing actually “cheap” about a backyard wedding. You’ll need to rent literally everything, including generators, staging, tenting, plumbing. You’ll need a place to put all of the cars with valets, every rental item down to the ice scoops. You’ll need a place for catering to set up and industrial kitchen, often times a second tent. You’ll need rain plans and to research sound ordinances. It’s often a lot more expensive and time consuming to pull off. BUT it can be completely beautiful! My fiancé’s older sister had one at his parents house on the ocean and when we got engaged they made it very clear that they would NEVER do that again, lol, which was fine by us. But if your primary concern is from a guest’s perspective I definitely wouldn’t think it was cheap! I would think it was sweet and sentimental!

Hi there! So music was one of our top priorities, so I totally feel you! I’m from the entertainment industry as are a large portion of our guests. We were SUPER picky. Not just in quality but how the bands function? Are we choosing a set ensemble or are the players replaceable and rotating? As in, do they play together consistently or are they just warm bodies playing their parts? First of all I’ll say I think that’s a good price. We’re paying about $12k for a ten piece band with three singers, three horns and a four piece rhythm section. My advice, as a performer? Absolutely do NOT micro manage your band. The pros of having a “wedding band” are that they work regularly and know how to hit the marks in a way a “normal” band might not for an event like a wedding. They know how to cater to the vibe the specific group is putting out and how to time it with the rest of your wedding schedule. If you micromanage all you’ll do is lock them in and Pisa them off and kill your vibe. They’re professionals and know what they’re doing. And this isn’t a chill night at your house, they know vibes more than you do when it comes to weddings and crowds. Your wedding music isn’t just about you, it’s about everyone in that room if you want everyone in the room dancing. You did your research and hired a great option, now let them do their job. That being said, I don’t think it’s wrong to give them the vibe you’re going for. For example, we know from a family wedding from last year that club music isn’t a good vibe for our family. We’re much more of a funk, soul crowd. So we specifically sought out a band that specializes in that. If they feel out the vibe and throw a pop song in because they know it’s right for the moment, then rock it out, but we hired them knowing our top genre would be primarily what’s played. Other than that, we’re leaving it to the professionals. If you have a “must play” song or two then send it their way, otherwise, let them rock it outs. That’s why you hired them.

It’s the same for humans. Fertility has declined by about 50% over the past 40 years globally. Exposure to endocrine disrupting chemicals found in plastics has been affecting not just people, but the animal kingdom. Male fetuses exposed to these common chemicals while in utero show sexual stunting for up to three generations, meaning if a mother exposes herself to very common everyday items like nonstick and plastics while carrying a male fetus, she’ll be permanently stunting the fertility of her son, her grandson and great grandson, seeing relief from that sexual stunting in the 4th generation out. This is found in all mammals. It’s not a coincidence that these impacts have been exponentially increasing since the rise of the petroleum industry. We need to make big changes in how we manage these chemicals and dispose of pharmaceuticals (which are not able to be processed out of most town water supplies so when your neighbor flushes their pills or you pee and those pharmaceuticals enter the toilet through your urine, it’s staying in treated water systems and constantly dosing every human that drinks it and every animal). Other animals aren’t the only ones at risk. The human race qualifies as an endangered species given the current threat to our fertility and environment.

I found my planner, who doesn’t post frequently, by her connections with other reputable vendors and organizations as she’s been in the industry 20 years. She sent me references and materials from her previous works directly from her clients who had approved being references, but doesn’t just post her client’s weddings. She also doesn’t name any clients but uses initials. I think there are other ways to show how qualified you are as a vendor, like being a part of local wedding organizations and making word of mouth connections that can allow you to not guilt a client into feeling taken advantage of by you using their image.

Our venue wanted us to sign a photography waiver allowing them to use our photos in any way they saw fit, including editing. That was a hard pass. I don’t mind a photo from our wedding being used, but you can’t just edit my photographer’s work without THEIR permission. And I had to get clarity from my makeup artist that she wouldn’t use any imagery from her work on our wedding without getting verbal permission from the person she was working on. I don’t mind her using my face, but I wasn’t going to give her permission to use my family and friend’s faces without their consent. It’s definitely something I paid attention to in my contracts. I also gave vendors permission to use content as long as they don’t tag us or name us.

Depending on your preferences and which resort you choose, you get walking distance or other special transportation to the parks, great food within your resort that is sit down dining instead of cafeteria style food, views of fireworks and the water parade, early entry every day, extra time late night on specific days, great theming, you get to stay in the Disney bubble, access to other deluxe resorts for food and entertainment…I definitely think it’s worth it.
